title: Continuity requires slow features relative to small-scale random changes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Continuity requires slow features relative to small-scale random changes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Continuous large-scale behavior can arise in a system with discrete components only when there are features that evolve slowly relative to the rate of small-scale random changes; for growth, the random small-scale changes must occur much faster than the overall growth.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 7: Mechanisms in Programs and Nature

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In general the point is that continuous behavior can arise in systems with discrete components only when there are features that evolve slowly relative to the rate of small-scale random changes.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 7, “Mechanisms in Programs and Nature”; section “The Phenomenon of Continuity” (from p. 327), p. 333. Scope: discrete systems with randomness, including growth processes and domain coarsening

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch07-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Timescale ratios and coarse-grained smoothness are measurable once a model ensemble and observables are fixed. Existing software supports broad computational searches, but no finite enumeration resolves an unrestricted only-when principle. Results can therefore test substantial restricted classes, not the full scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For a defined ensemble of discrete stochastic systems, estimate microscopic decorrelation, macroscopic feature, and growth timescales and test whether smooth coarse-grained trajectories occur only when the first is much shorter. Any robust counterexample with continuous macroscopic behavior but no timescale separation would refute the necessity claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Continuous behavior and relevant feature lack unique definitions.

The claim ranges over an unbounded class of systems.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The timescale comparison is a well-posed simulation inside the growth and coarsening models named in the section. A sample can refute a claimed necessary condition, but it cannot establish the condition for every discrete system. Coverage of the full general principle is therefore only partial.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In ensembles of discrete growth and coarsening models, vary the ratio of the small-scale mixing time to the large-scale growth time and measure a continuity statistic of the large-scale interface. A sharp loss of continuity below a modest timescale separation would support the proposed necessary condition inside those ensembles; continuity without that separation would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Continuous, slow, and random each need a definition before the threshold is meaningful.

The universal quantifier over every discrete system is not settled by any finite ensemble.
